o1.biggest_strength: It leads with the right return-reducing facts: 5 to 12 cards, about 10 flat notes, real thickness numbers, snug first-week slots and the small coin-pouch trade-off.
o1.biggest_mistake: It implies the wallet is about 14 mm thick with 12 cards plus about 10 notes, when the brief only supports 14 mm with 12 cards.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fix the unsupported thickness and hidden-pocket note claims, tighten the SEO title under 60 characters, and keep the rest largely as written.

o2.biggest_strength: It uses the actual customer doubts and return drivers well: cash capacity appears repeatedly as a number, the break-in issue is explained, and the FAQ mirrors the top page questions.
o2.biggest_mistake: The extra strategy and measurement sections are useful internally but would need to be stripped before handing the copy straight to the web team.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Move the snug first-week card-slot expectation into an above-the-fold bullet or the add-to-cart line, and remove the internal rationale from the final page copy handoff.

reason: Output 2 is the one I would rather pay for because it is just as on-brand but cleaner on the numbers, especially avoiding the unsupported 14 mm claim with cash included. It also shows it understood why the copy choices matter for cash-related returns and early tight-slot returns.
